la:adj:incolumis.html:
in-cŏlŭmis, e (
abl. sing. regularly incolumi; incolume, Pomp. and Cic. ap. P.), adj., unimpaired, uninjured, in good condition, still alive, safe, sound, entire, whole (class. and freq.; syn.: salvus, intactus, integer): urbem et cives integros incolumesque servavi,: salvum atque incolumem exercitum transducere,; cf. ; : ut haec retinere per populum Romanum incolumia ac salva possimus, id. Div. ap. Caccil. 22, 72: ut salvae et incolumes sint civitates,: valeant cives mei: sint incolumes, sint florentes, sint beati,: aliquem in omni honore incolumem habere,; : sortium beneficio se esse incolumem,: incolumes ad unum omnes in castra perveniunt,: quo stante et incolume, ap. P.; cf.: incolume illo, Pomp. Fragm. ib.: omnibus navibus ad unam incolumibus milites exposuit,: ita ut sit data Incolumem (dotem) sistere ei,: argentum hoc actutum incolume redigam,: (arx) incolumis atque intacta,: incolumes non redeunt genae,: nulla incolumi relicta re,: aedes,. — With ab: a calamitate judicii,: audacia,unshaken, unsubdued,.—Comp.: deteriores sunt incolumiores, Quadrig. ap. .—Sup. and adv. do not occur.

la:noun:incolumitas.html:
incŏlŭmĭtas, ātis, f.
incolumis
,
good condition, soundness, safety (class.): incolumitas est salutis tuta atque integra conservatio,: in incolumitate,: concordi populo et omnia referenti ad incolumitatem et ad libertatem suam, ; cf.: incolumitatem ac libertatem retinere,: deditis pollicebatur,: mundi,— In plur., ; .

la:verb:incido.html:
incīdo, cīdi, cīsum, 3, v. a.
in-caedo
,
to cut into, cut through, cut open, cut up (class.).
Lit.: teneris arboribus incisis atque inflexis,: arbores,; : inciditur vitro, lapide, osseisve cultellis,; cf.: palmes inciditur in medullam,: venam,to open,; ; ; cf.: incisi nervi,: circa vulnus scalpello,: pinnas,to clip,; so, vites falce,: pulmo incisus,cut up, divided,; cf.: eupatoria foliis per extremitates incisis,i. e. notched, indented,: nos linum incidimus, legimus,cut through, cut,: funem,: corpora mortuorum, to dissect, Cels. praef.: nocentes homines vivos,: quid habet haruspex cur pulmo incisus etiam in bonis extis dirimat tempus?: si rectum limitem rupti torrentibus pontes inciderint,cut through, broken through,: squamisque incisus adaestuat amnis,: non incisa notis marmcra publicis,engraved,: tabula ... his ferme incisa litteris fuit,—
Transf.
To cut in, to carve, engrave, inscribe on any thing; usually constr. with in and abl.; less freq. with in and acc., the dat., or absol.
With in and abl.: id non modo tum scripserunt, verum etiam in aere incisum nobis tradiderunt,; cf.: foedus in columna aenea incisum et perscriptum,; : in qua basi grandibus litteris P. Africani nomen erat incisum,, § 74: nomina in tabula incisa,: notum est carmen incisum in sepulcro,; ; : incidens litteras in fago recenti,: indicem in aeneis tabulis,: quae vos incidenda in aere censuistis,.—
With in and acc.: quae (acta) ille in aes incidit,: leges in aes incisae,: lege jam in aes incisā,: quod ita erit gestum, lex erit, et in aes incidi jubebitis credo illa legitima: consules populum jure rogaverunt, etc.,.—
With dat. (poet. and post-Aug.): verba ceris,: amores arboribus,: fastos marmoreo parieti,: nomen non trabibus aut saxis,; cf.: primum aliquid da, quod possim titulis incidere,i. e. among your titles,.—
Absol.: incidebantur jam domi leges,; cf.: tabula his litteris incīsa,: sine delectu morum quisquis incisus est,inscribed, registered,: Victorem litteris incisis appellare,.—
To make by

cutting, to cut (rare): ferroque incidit acuto Perpetuos dentes et serrae repperit usum,: novas incide faces, tibi ducitur uxor,; .

Trop.
To break off, interrupt, put an end to: poëma ad Caesarem, quod institueram, incidi,have broken off, stopped,: inciditur omnis jam deliberatio, si intellegitur non posse fieri, ?*!; cf. : tandem haec singultu verba incidente profatur,: novas lites,: ludum,: vocis genus crebro incidens,broken, interrupted,.—
To cut off, cut short, take away, remove: media,to cut short,: qui mihi pinnas inciderant nolunt easdem renasci,: Tarquinius spe omni reditus incisā exsulatum Tusculum abiit,cut off,: spe incisā,; ; cf. ; : tantos actus,: ipsam, quam promimus horam casus incidit,: testamentum,to annul, invalidate,.—
In rhet., to make by cutting, to cut: aequaliter particulas,.— Hence,
incī-sum, i, n., rhet. t. t. for the Gr. κόμμα,a section or division of a sentence, a clause: quae nescio cur, cum Graeci κόμματα et κῶλα nominent, nos non recte incisa et membra dicamus, (for which: incisiones et membra,): incisum erit sensus non expleto numero conclusus, plerisque pars membri,; cf. ; 32; 44; 67; 123.—
incīsē, adv., in short clauses: quo pacto deceat incise membratimve dici,; cf. incisim.

la:verb:incumbo.gloss: to lay oneself upon; to lean or recline on something
senses: to lay oneself upon; to lean or recline on something
to press down on, fall upon (e.g. one's sword)
to bend one's attention to; to devote or apply oneself to
la:verb:incumbo.html:
incumbo, cŭbŭi, cŭbĭtum, ĕre, v. n.
1. incubo
,
to lay one's self upon, to lean or recline upon a thing (cf. ingruo; class., partic. in the trop. sense).
Lit., constr. with in, ad, super, or dat.; also with the simple acc.: olivae,: in parietem,: densis ordinibus nunc alii in alios, nunc in scuta incumbentes sustinebant impetus Romanorum,: toro,: materiae,: terrae,: super praedam,to lie upon,: in eum,: ad vos, 9, 385: cumulatis in aqua sarcinis insuper incumbebant,: validis incumbere remis,; ; .—Of the heavens: cava in se convexitas vergit, et cardini suo, hoc est terrae, undique incumbit,: mare,to cast itself into the sea,: fessi arma sua, ap. : tecto incubuit bubo,perched on,: gladium faciam culcitam, camque incumbam,.—
Transf., to lean or incline towards, to overhang; to rush towards: silex prona jugo laevum incumbebat ad amnem,: laurus incumbens arae,: in gladium, to fall on one's sword, : gladio,: ferro,: in hostem,to press upon the enemy,; cf.: duo duces circumstare urbem ... et unum in locum totam periculi molem, omne onus incubuisse,.—
Trop.
To press upon, burden, oppress, weigh upon: incubuere (venti) mari,: tempestas a vertice silvis incubuit,: gravis incumbens scopulis aestas,: febrium terris incubuit cohors,: (aestus) incubuit populo,. —Absol.: saevior armis Luxuria incubuit,.—
To bend one's attention to, to apply or devote one's self to, to exert one's self, or take pains with, pay attention to; constr. with in, ad, or dat.: rogandis legibus,: ceris et stilo,: labori,: toto pectore novae cogitationi,: et animo et opibus in bellum,: ut jam inclinato (judici) reliqua incumbat oratio,press upon, exert influence on,; cf.: invidia mihi incumbit,: in aliquod studium,: in causam,: acrius graviusque ad ulciscendas rei publicae injurias,: tota mente in aliquam curam et cogitationem,: toto pectore ad laudem,: omni cogitatione curaque in rem publicam,: fato urguenti incumbere,to press on, hasten,.—With inf.: sarcire ruinas,: delatorem pervertere,.—With ut and subj.: Appius Claudius ... cum suis tum totius nobilitatis viribus incubuit, ut, etc.,.— Absol.: nunc, nunc incumbere tempus,.—
To incline, choose, be inclined to, lean towards: hoc servi esse officium reor, ... non quo incumbat eum (i. e. erum) inpellere,: ut eos, qui audiunt, quocumque incubuerit, possit impellere,whithersoever he may incline, choose,: eodem incumbunt municipia,are inclined the same way,: ad voluntatem perferendae legis,: voluntatum inclinatio ad virum bonum,to lean towards, turn to,: in causam, Cael. ad : in cupiditatem,: in illo,.—
To be incumbent upon one as a duty (post-class.): accusandi necessitas domino,: ei probatio,: judici omnium rerum officium,.

la:adj:incautus.gloss: incautious, heedless, reckless, unsuspecting, improvident, in one’s ignorance, not careful, careless
senses: incautious, heedless, reckless, unsuspecting, improvident, in one’s ignorance, not careful, careless
unforeseen, unexpected, unguarded against, off one’s guard
la:adj:incautus.html:
in-cautus, a, um, adj.
Act., incautious, heedless, improvident, inconsiderate (class.; syn. improvidus): ut in ipsum incautum atque etiam imparatum incideret,; : Trebonius oppressus est ab hoste incautus,; ; : minime incautus patronus,: ab secundis rebus incauti,: ad credendum pavor,. — Comp.: incautior fuissem, nisi, etc.,: juventa,. — Sup.: incautissimus quia credulus,. —
With ab, or the gen.: a fraude,: futuri,: sui,. —
Pass., not guarded against or that cannot be guarded against, unforeseen, unexpected, uncertain, dangerous (not in ante-Aug. prose): scelus,; cf.: sic est incautum quidquid habetur amor, (v. 24 M.): quod neglexeris incautum at que apertum habes,: iter hostibus,: sub ictu,: tenebrae,.— Hence, adv.: in-cautē, incautiously, inconsiderately: adhuc stulte omnia et incaute,: atque inconsulte pugnare. .— Comp.: quod paulo incautius custodias in muro dispositas videbat,: sequi,: subit murum,: potes apparatius cenare apud multos: nusquam hilarius, simplicius, incautius,more at ease,.— Sup.: ut se ipsos incautissime proderent, Aug. de Mor. Manich. fin.

la:adj:inconstans.html:
in-constans, antis, adj.,
inconstant, changeable, fickle, capricious, inconsistent (class.).
Of persons: mihi ridicule es visus esse inconstans, qui eundem et laederes, et laudares,: populus in omnibus inconstantissimus,.—
Of inanim. and abstr. things: inconstans est, quod ab eodem de eadem re diverse dicitur,: litterae,: venti,: medendi arte nulla inconstantior,: quid inconstantius Deo?. — Sup.: inconstantissimo vultu et maestissimo,.—Adv.: inconstanter, inconstantly, capriciously, inconsistently: jactantibus se opinionibus inconstanter et turbide,inconsistently and confusedly,: loqui,: haec dicuntur inconstantissime,without the least consistency,: adductus primo ita negare inconstanter, ut, etc.,: prodire,: agens, M. Aurel. ap. , ep. 2.

la:adj:incredibilis.html:
incrēdĭbĭlis, e, adj.
2. in-credo
.
Pass.
That cannot be believed, incredible, extraordinary, unparalleled (class.): fides,: quaedam et prope singularis et divina vis ingenii,: voluptas,: foedus sceleris,: furor,: rem facere incredibilem,: incredibilia probabilibus intexere,: incredibile est,it is incredible,: praeter spem atque incredibile hoc mihi obtigit,unforeseen,: incredibile est, quanta me molestia affecerit,; so . —With inf.: incredibile est, a filio patrem occisum,: incredibilem in modum concursus fiunt,: incredibile quantum coaluere,—With sup. in u (not in Cic.): incredibile memoratu est, quam facile coaluerint,.—
Not worthy of belief, or that is not believed (ante-class.), . —
Act., unbelieving, incredulous (post-class.): incredibiles cogentur credere,.— Hence, adv.: incrēdĭbĭlĭter, incredibly, extraordinarily (class.): quibus ego incredibiliter delector,: consentire,: pertimuit,.

la:adj:incertus.html:
incertus, a, um (archaic
gen. plur. incertūm, Pac. ap. ), adj.
2. incertus; hence, acc. to certus
.
Object., of things whose (external or internal) qualities are not firmly established, uncertain, unsettled, doubtful, untrustworthy, not fast, not firm (class.): amicus certus in re incerta cernitur, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 428 Vahl.); cf. id. ap. (Trag. v. 12 Vahl.): incerti socii an hostes essent,: incertus (infans) masculus an femina esset,; cf. : cum incerta bellum an pax cum Celtiberis essent, Weissenb.: spe incerta certum mihi laborem sustuli, prol. alt. 9; : nuptiae,: aetas (puerilis) maxime lubrica atque incerta,: itinera,: dominatus,: status,: sedes,: ambiguae testis incertaeque rei,: comarum Anulus incertā non bene fixus acu,not fast,: colligere incertos et in ordine ponere crines,dishevelled,: per incertam lunam sub luce maligna,not clearly visible, dim,: soles,: securis,that did not strike with a sure blow,: vultus,disturbed, uneasy,: ille vitam suam ad incertissimam spem reservavit,: arbori incertae nullam prudentia cani Rectoris cum ferret opem, the ship uncertain in her course, because no longer obeying the helm, Halm. — In neutr. ellipt.: clauserant portas incertum vi an voluntate,; — Neutr. as adv. (poet.): incertum vigilans,; . —
Subject., as respects one's perceptions or convictions, not firmly established, uncertain, undetermined, doubtful, dubious (so most freq. in prose and poetry): nihil est incertius vulgo,: casus,: ut alia certa, alia incerta esse dicunt,; cf.: est igitur ridiculum, quod est dubium, id relinquere incertum, id. Mur. 32, 68; and: incerta atque dubia,: ut incertis temporibus diversisque itineribus iretur,; so, eventus reliqui temporis,: exitus pugnarum,: adulterium,: auctor,: cujus ora puellares faciunt incerta capilli,make the sex doubtful,: incerta persona heres institui non potest,; ; cf. 2, 238.—
With rel. or interrog.-clause: nunc mihi incertumst, abeam an maneam,: moriendum certe est, et id incertum, an hoc ipso die,; cf. : (Gallus) avem, an gentem, an nomen, an fortunam corporis significet, incertum est,: confessus est quidem sed incertum, utrum quia verum erat, an quia, etc.,: neque plane occultati humilitate arborum et tamen incerti, quidnam esset, Kritz.—Abl. absol.: multi annantes navibus incerto prae tenebris, quid aut peterent aut vitarent, foede interierunt,.—
Subst.: incer-tum, i, n., an uncertainty: quicquid incerti mihi in animo prius aut ambiguum fuit, Nunc liquet, nunc defaecatum est,: ne cujus incerti vanique auctor esset,: incerta maris et tempestatum,: incerta fortunae experiri,: incerta belli,: bona, fortunae possessionesque omnium in dubium incertumque revocabuntur,; cf. : Minucius praefectus annonae in incertum creatus,for an indefinite time,: postremo fugere an manere tutius foret, in incerto erat,: Allobroges diu in incerto habuere, quidnam consilii caperent,; cf. : imperia ducum in incerto reliquerat,—
Transf., of a person who is in a state of uncertainty respecting any thing, uncertain, in uncertainty, hesitating, doubtful: quo ego ope mea Pro incertis certos compotesque consili Dimitto, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 188 Vahl.): nolo suspensam et incertam plebem Romanam obscura spe et caeca exspectatione pendere,; so, varius incertusque agitabat,; : ego certe me incerto scio hoc daturum nemini homini,.—
With rel.-clause: quid dicam hisce, incertus sum,: cum incertus essem, ubi esses,: incerti ignarique, quid potissimum facerent,: incerti quidnam esset,: incertus, quonam modo aciem instrueret,: incerti, quo fata ferant, ubi sistere detur,: incertus, Geniumne loci famulumne parentis Esse putet,: faber, incertus scamnum faceretne Priapum,.—
With gen. (not in Cic.): summarum rerum incerti, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 187 Vahl.): incertusque meae paene salutis eram,: sententiae,: veri,; : rerum,: ultionis,: sui,: naves incertae locorum, Auct. B. Afr. 7: mox incertus animi, fesso corpore, etc.,; : futurorum,: consilii,.—
With abl.: incerti metu,.—(ε) With de and abl.: incertus de salute alicujus,.—Hence, adv. in two forms: incertē and incerto (both ante-class.), uncertainly, not certainly, dubiously: incerte errat animus, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 259 Vahl.): vagat exsul, Pac. ap. (Trag. Rel. p. 87 Rib.): ubi Habitet dum incerto scio,: incerto scio,: incerto autumo,.

With abl.: incerti metu,.—(ε) With de and abl.: incertus de salute alicujus,.—Hence, adv. in two forms: incertē and incerto (both ante-class.), uncertainly, not certainly, dubiously: incerte errat animus, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 259 Vahl.): vagat exsul, Pac. ap. (Trag. Rel. p. 87 Rib.): ubi Habitet dum incerto scio,: incerto scio,: incerto autumo,.

la:verb:incipio.html:
incĭpĭo, cēpi, ceptum, 3 (archaic incepsit inceperit, Paul. ex Müll.), v. a. and n. [in-capio; lit., to seize upon, lay hold of; opp. to desinere; hence, with the accessory idea of action),
to begin to do something, to take in hand (syn. incoho; in class. prose, viz. in Cic., only in the tempp. press., while coepi is used in the tempp. perff.); constr. usually with the inf., less freq. absol., with the acc., ab, or adv. of place or time.
Act.
With inf.: ut homines mortem vel optare incipiant vel certe timere desistant,: huic incipio sententiae diffidere,: prius quam incipit tinnire,: bella gerere,: leges neglegere,: queri cum multis incipiunt,: nimis cito diligere,: amare aliquem,: fossas complere,: rem frumentariam expedire,: triplicem aciem ducere,; 2, 30, 1: cum maturescere frumenta inciperent,; cf. : cum primum pabuli copia esse inciperet,; cf.: ictus erat, qua crus esse incipit,; ; : opes pellere dominatione,: si res explicare incipiam,: Bessus agere gratias incipit,: cenare,: promovere scalas,: si dormire incipis ortu luciferi,: male quod mulier facere incepit, nisi id efficere perpetrat, etc.... Si bene facere incepit, etc. (shortly afterward, occeperunt), and 14: satis nequam sum, utpote qui hodie inceperim Amare,.—
Absol.: ut incipiendi ratio fuerit, ita sit desinendi modus,; cf. ; : dum incipimus,: dum deliberamus, quando incipiendum sit, incipere jam serum est,: in incipiendo, etc.,: ac statim sic rex incipit, thus begins (to speak), ; cf.: nec sic incipies, ut scriptor cyclicus olim: Fortunam Priami, etc.,: sic incipit, with a foll. direct quotation,; ; and simply incipit,: sapere aude, Incipe,make a beginning, begin,; : priusquam incipias, consulto opus est,: turpe inceptu est,: incipientes atque adhuc teneri (pueri),who are beginning to learn, beginners,: incipiens,; ; prooem. § 1; 3; 10, 7, 18: quoties madidum ver incipit, —
With acc. (once in Cic., once in Cæs., v.infra): facinus audax incipit,: facinus,: pugilatum,: iter,: aliquid novi negotii,: bellum (opp. deponere),: tam prava,: indigna nobis,: opus,: bellum,; ; : sementem,: Maenalios versus,: si id facere non potueris, quod, ut opinio mea fert, ne incipies quidem,; : iter mihi incepi,: tantum incepi operis,: mandata,; : auspicia a parricidio,: multa, Cat. ap. .— Pass.: tanta incepta res est,: nuptiarum gratia haec sunt ficta atque incepta,; : si inceptam oppugnationem reliquissent,: quia dici extremum erat, proelium non inceptum,: proelium incipitur,; 74, 2: saxis proelium incipitur,: satis cito incipi victoriam,; ; ; fin.: iter inceptum celerant,: inceptumque decurre laborem,: inceptum frustra summitte furorem,: deus me vetat Inceptos iambos Ad umbilicum adducere,: in re incipiunda ad defendendam noxiam,: in contentionibus aut incipiendis aut finiendis,: a tantis princeps incipiendus erat,.—
With ab or an adv. of place or time: a Jove incipiendum putat, (acc. to the Gr. of Aratus, ἐκ Διὸς ἀρχώμεσθα): ab illis incipit uxor,; : incipiamus ab iis,: semper ab excusatione aetatis incipientem,: potissimum incipiam ab ea parte,: optime manus a sinistra parte incipit, in dextra deponitur,: amicitia incepta a parvis cum aetate accrevit simul,.— Pass. impers.: optime incipitur a longis, recte aliquando a brevibus,.
Neutr., to begin to be, to begin, commence (rare but class.); constr. with abl. instrum., or absol.
With abl.: tertius sinus Acrocerauniis incipit montibus,: censere ut principium anni inciperet mense Decembri,: verbum petere quo incipiant,.—
Absol.: cum ver esse coeperat ... cum rosam viderat, tum incipere ver arbitrabatur,: quoties incipit sensus aut desinit,: hic annus incipit vicesimus,: narrationis incipit mihi initium,: jam tum inceperat turba inter eos,: tempus erat quo prima quies mortalibus aegris Incipit,: mox Idumaea incipit et Palaestina,: epistula, quam incipiente febricula scripseras,: incipientes curas principis onerari,: incipiens adhuc et nondum adulta seditio,: incipiens omnia sentit amor,: Menander Syracusanus incipientis juventae,: incipiente aestate,: trixago incipientibus hydropicis efficax,: quem (honorem) et incipientes principes et desinentes adeo concupis cunt ut auferant,.—Hence, in-ceptum, i, n., a beginning, attempt, undertaking (freq. in historians and poets, but not in Cæs.; also rare in Cic.): cujus ego non modo factum, sed inceptum ullum conatumve contra patriam deprehendero,: servetur ad imum, Qualis ab incepto processerit (persona),from the beginning onwards,: permanere in incepto, Luccei. ap. : a quo incepto studioque me ambitio mala detinuerat,: cujus neque consilium neque inceptum ullum frustra erat,; cf.: ni ea res longius nos ab incepto traheret,the subject,fin.: absistere incepto,: desistere incepto,: haerere in incepto,: peragere inceptum,; cf.: perficere inceptum,: piget incepti,: nunc ad inceptum redeo,; : turpe inceptum est,.— In plur.: cupidus incepta patrandi,: juventus Catilinae inceptis favebat,: incepta mea inpedivit,; cf.: inceptis annue, diva, meis,; and: di nostra incepta secundent,: gravia et magna professa,.
la:verb:incipio.inflection: cēpi, ceptum, 3, v. a. and n.

la:verb:inclino.gloss: to cause to lean, bend, tilt, incline, turn; bend down, bow something; divert; swerve
senses: to cause to lean, bend, tilt, incline, turn; bend down, bow something; divert; swerve
to cause to fall back or give way, drive back
to change, alter; abase, cause to decline, bring down
to sink, droop, turn, incline, decline, bend
to be favorably disposed towards something, incline to
la:verb:inclino.html:
in-clīno, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. and n.
clino, clinatus
.
Act., to cause to lean, bend, incline, turn a thing in any direction; to bend down, bow a thing.
Lit.
In gen. (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose): vela contrahit malosque inclinat,: genua arenis,: (rector maris) omnes Inclinavit aquas ad avarae litora Trojae,: inclinato in dextrum capite,; : inclinata utrolibet cervix,: pollice intus inclinato,: arbor Inclinat varias pondere nigra comas,: sic super Actaeas agilis Cyllenius arces Inclinat cursus,: at mihi non oculos quisquam inclinavit euntes,i. e. closed my sinking eyes,(Müll. inclamavit euntis): prius sol meridie se inclinavit, quam, etc.,i. e. declined,; cf.: inclinato jam in postmeridianum tempus die,.— Mid.: inclinari ad judicem (opp. reclinari ad suos,): (terra) inclinatur retroque recellit,bends down,: saxa inclinatis per humum quaesita lacertis,.—
In partic.
In milit. lang., to cause to fall back or give way: ut Hostus cecidit, confestim Romana inclinatur acies,i. e. loses ground, retreats,: tum inclinari rem in fugam apparuit,: quasdam acies inclinatas jam et labantes,; cf. under II. —
In gen., to turn back, cause to move backward: septemtrio inclinatum stagnum eodem quo aestus ferebat,: cum primum aestu fretum inclinatum est,.—
In mal. part., to lie down, stretch out: jam inclinabo me cum liberta tua,: quot discipulos inclinet Hamillus,: ipsos maritos,.—
Transf., of color, to incline to: colore ad aurum inclinato,: coloris in luteum inclinati,.—
Of a disease, to abate, diminish: morbus inclinatus,: febris se inclinat, al.—
Trop.
In gen., to turn or incline a person or thing in any direction: se ad Stoicos,: culpam in aliquem,to lay the blame upon,: quo se fortuna, eodem etiam favor hominum inclinat,: judicem inclinat miseratio,moves,: haec animum inclinant, ut credam, etc.,.—Mid.: quamquam inclinari opes ad Sabinos, rege inde sumpto videbantur,.—
In partic.
To change, alter, and esp. for the worse, to bring down, abase, cause to decline: se fortuna inclinaverat,: omnia simul inclinante fortuna,: ut me paululum inclinari timore viderunt, sic impulerunt,to give way, yield,: eloquentiam,.—
To throw upon, remove, transfer: haec omnia in dites a pauperibus inclinata onera,: omnia onera, quae communia quondam fuerint, inclinasse in primores civitatis,.—In gram., to form or inflect a word by a change of termination (postclass.): (vinosus aut vitiosus) a vocabulis, non a verbo inclinata sunt,; ; : partim hoc in loco adverbium est, neque in casus inclinatur,.—
Neutr., to bend, turn, incline, decline, sink.
Lit. (rare, and not in Cic.): paulum inclinare necesse est corpora,: sol inclinat,: inclinare meridiem sentis, (for which: sol se inclinavit,; v. above I. A. 1.): in vesperam inclinabat dies,.—
In partic., in milit. lang., to yield, give way: ita conflixerunt, ut aliquamdin in neutram partem inclinarent acies,: in fugam,: inclinantes jam legiones,; .—
To change for the worse, turn, fail: si fortuna belli inclinet,: inde initia magistratuum nostrum meliora ferme, et finis inclinat,. —
Trop., to incline to, be favorably disposed towards any thing (also in Cic.): si se dant et sua sponte quo impellimus, inclinant et propendent, etc.,: ecquid inclinent ad meum consilium adjuvandum,: ad voluptatem audientium,: in stirpem regiam studiis,: amicus dulcis, Cum mea compenset vitiis bona, pluribus hisce ... inclinet,: cum sententia senatus inclinaret ad pacem cum Pyrrho foedusque faciendum,: color ad crocum inclinans,: omnia repente ad Romanos inclinaverunt. turned in favor of, . — With ut: ut belli causa dictatorem creatum arbitrer, inclinat animus,: multorum eo inclinabant sententiae, ut tempus pugnae differretur,: hos ut sequar inclinat animus,. — With inf.: inclinavit sententia, suum in Thessaliam agmen demittere,: inclinavit sententia universos ire,; cf. .— Pass.: consules ad patrum causam inclinati,; cf.: inclinatis ad suspicionem mentibus,: inclinatis ad credendum animis,; : ad paenitentiam,. —
In partic., to change, alter from its former condition (very rare): inclinant jam fata ducum,change,. — Hence, in-clīnātus, a, um, P. a.
Bent down, sunken: senectus,; of the voice, low, deep: vox,; cf.: inclinata ululantique voce more Asiatico canere,. —
Inclined, disposed, prone to any thing: plebs ante inclinatior ad Poenos fuerat,: plebs ad regem Macedonasque,: ipsius imperatoris animus ad pacem inclinatior erat,; .—
Sunken, fallen, deteriorated: ab excitata fortuna ad inclinatam et prope jacentem desciscere,: copiae,.—In neutr. plur. subst.: rerum inclinata ferre,i. e. troubles, misfortunes,.
la:verb:inclino.inflection: āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. and n.

la:verb:incurso.gloss: to run to or against, dash or strike against; assault, attack, charge at
senses: to run to or against, dash or strike against; assault, attack, charge at
to fall upon, assault a woman carnally
la:verb:incurso.html:
incurso, āvi, ātum, 1,
v. freq. n. and a. [incurro], to run to or against, to dash or strike against, to assault, attack (class.).
Lit.
With in: jam in vos incursabimus,: in agmen Romanum,.—
With the simple acc.: aliquem pugnis,to pitch into,: (me) boves incursent cornibus,: ubi vivos homines mortui incursant boves (meaning raw hides as whips), : agros Romanos,to make an incursion into,; ; : latera,.—In pass.: agmen incursatum ab equitibus hostium,; .—With dat.: silvasque tenent delphines, et altis Incursant ramis,: rupibus incursat,runs against the rocks,.—
In partic., to fall upon, assault a woman carnally (post - class.): nuptam alienam,.—
Transf.: ea, quae oculis vel auribus incursant,that strike, meet them,; cf.: pleraque in oculos incurrunt,: incurrit haec nostra laurus in oculos,: lana ovis nigrae, cui nullus alius color incursaverit,is intermixed,.—
Trop.: incursabit in te dolor meus,: in omnes amicos atque inimicos, notos atque ignotos,.

la:verb:includo.gloss: to shut up or in, confine, enclose, imprison, keep in
senses: to shut up or in, confine, enclose, imprison, keep in
to include, enclose or insert something, incorporate
la:verb:includo.html:
in-clūdo, si, sum, 3, v. a.
claudo
,
to shut up, shut in, confine, enclose, imprison, keep in (class.).—Constr. with in and abl., in and acc., rarely with the simple abl., dat., or absol.
Lit.
With in and abl.: habemus senatusconsultum inclusum in tabulis, tamquam in vagina reconditum,: armatos in cella Concordiae,: in uno cubiculo,: in curia,; : omne animal in mundo intus,: dum sumus inclusi in his compagibus corporis,: consule in carcere incluso,; cf.: avis inclusa in cavea,; cf.: (Animus) inclusus in corpore,: veriti, ne includerentur vento in hostium orā,weather-bound on the coast,.—
With in and acc.: aliquem in custodias,: aliquem in carcerem,—
With the simple abl.: inclusi parietibus,; cf.: aliquem carcere,: vim terrae cavernis,; : inclusus caveā,: minora castra inclusa majoribus,; cf. fin.: grandes zmaragdos auro,i. e. to set,; cf.: suras auro,to sheathe,; : inclusus carcere nassae,caught,.—
With dat.: corpora furtim Includunt caeco lateri,: publicae custodiae aliquem,, ext. 3.—(ε) Absol., or with acc.: inclusum atque abditum latere in occulto,: fila numerata porri,: intrat positas inclusa per aequora moles,: pars Heracleae incluserunt sese,; for which: Aetolorum utraeque manus Heracleam sese incluserunt,: si quis alienum hominem aut pecudem incluserit et fame necaverit,.—Poet.: huc aliena ex arbore germen Includunt,ingraft,. —
Transf.
To obstruct, hinder, stop up (rare, and mostly post-Aug.): dolor includit vocem,: consuli primo tam novae rei admiratio incluserat vocem,: spiritum,; : lacrimas (dolor),: os alicui insertā spongiā, Sen. de Ira, 3, 10: post inclusum volatum,; cf. 7, 5, 4.—
To bound, limit: Asiam in duas partes Agrippa divisit: unam inclusit ab oriente Phrygia . . . alteram determinavit ab oriente Armenia minore, etc.,. —
Trop.
In gen., to include, enclose, insert in any thing.
With in and abl.: qua de re agitur illud, quod multis locis in jurisconsultorum includitur formulis,: similem sui speciem in clipeo Minervae,: animorum salus inclusa in ipsa est,.—
With in and acc.: in hujus me tu consilii societatem tamquam in equum Trojanum cum principibus includis?: quam (opinationem) in omnes definitiones superiores inclusimus,; : eos in eam formam,:

orationem in epistulam, ; .—

With abl. (freq. in Liv.): illa quae mihi sunt inclusa medullis,; cf. ; : oratio libro inclusa,: verba versu includere,: si aperias haec, quae verbo uno inclusa erant,; : antiquo me includere ludo quaeris,.—
With dat.: τοποθεσίαν quam postulas, includam orationi meae, ; cf. : quas aureae armillae inclusas gestavit,: portae,.— (ε) With adv. of place: intus inclusum periculum est,.—
In partic.
Of time, to close, finish, end (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): sic nobis, qui nunc magnum spiramus amantes, Forsitan includet crastina fata dies, (3, 7), 54; cf. : tempora quae semel Notis condita fastis Inclusit (= consignavit), volucris dies,; so, hujus actionem (vespera),: mellationem idibus Nov. fere,: omnes potiones aqua frigida,—
To restrain, control: adversus imperatorem, nullis neque temporis nec juris inclusum angustiis,.

la:adj:incommodus.html:
in-commŏdus, a, um, adj.,
inconvenient, unsuitable, unfit, unseasonable, troublesome, disagreeable.
Adj.
Of things (class. and freq.): iter,: res,: valetudo, Cic. : colloquium pro re nata non incommodum,: ne voce quidem incommodā,: severitas morum,: conflictatio turbae,; : eorum controversiam non incommodum videtur cum utrorumque ratione exponere,: naves propugnatoribus incommodae,.—Comp.: ut actori incommodior esset exhibitio,: incommodioris condicionis homines, Mos. et Rom. Leg. Coll. 15, 3, 1. — Sup.: in rebus ejus incommodissimis,. —
Of persons, troublesome (rare but class.): aliquid huic responde, commode, ne incommodus nobis sit, (but not in Bacch. 3, 2, 17; v. Ritschl ad h. l.): idem facilem et liberalem patrem incommodum esse amanti filio disputat,.—
Subst.: incommŏdum, i, n., inconvenience, trouble, disadvantage, detriment, injury, misfortune (freq. and class.): quom ejus incommodum tam aegre feras,: nostro incommodo detrimentoque, si est ita necesse, doleamus,: qui locus est talis, ut plus habeat adjumenti quam incommodi,: non modo incommodi nihil ceperunt, sed etiam ... in quaestu sunt versati,: timet, ne ipse aliquo afficiatur incommodo,: accidit repentinum incommodum: tanta enim tempestas cooritur, ut, etc.,: ab officio abduci incommodo,; cf. ellipt.: nec id incommodo tuo (sc. feceris),: quae res magnum nostris attulit incommodum,: quid iniquitas loci habeat incommodi,: si quid importetur nobis incommodi,: ex eo concursu navium magnum esse incommodum acceptum,; cf.: ut acceptum incommodum virtute sarciretur (shortly before: detrimentum acceptum),: reiciendi, deminuendi, devitandive incommodi causa,: incommodum inter eos (socios) commune est, loss (opp. lucrum), .—Rarely with gen. rei: commoveri incommodo valetudinis,; cf. morbi,.—In plur.: multis incommodis difficultatibusque affectus,; ; : tot incommodis conflictati,; .— With gen.: corporum,i. e. diseases,: pulmonum,: vesicae,: ferre incommoda vitae,. —
Adv.: incommŏdē, inconveniently, incommodiously, unfortunately, unseasonably: fores Hae sonitu suo moram mihi obiciunt incommode,; : posse pro re nata te non incommode ad me in Albanum venire,: accidit,: adversari,.—Comp.: cum illo quidem actum optime est: mecum incommodius,.— Sup.: incommodissime navigare,.

la:noun:incommodum.gloss: disadvantage, inconvenience, detriment, harm, setback, misfortune
senses: disadvantage, inconvenience, detriment, harm, setback, misfortune

la:verb:incommodo.html:
incommŏdo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. n. and a.
[id.].
Neutr., to occasion inconvenience or trouble to any one, to be inconvenient, troublesome, annoying (rare): alicui,: alicui nihil,; : ipsa scientia, etiam si incommodatura sit, gaudeant,; .— Pass. impers.: obnoxium eum dici, cui quid ab eo, cui esse obnoxius dicitur, incommodari et noceri potest,.—
Act., to render inconvenient or troublesome, to incommode (post-class.): si quid aliud fiat, quod navigationem incommodet, difficiliorem faciat, vel prorsus impediat,: si incommodatur ad usum manus,: usum,.
la:verb:incommodo.inflection: āvi, ātum, 1, v. n. and a.

la:verb:incoho.html:
incoho (better than inchŏo, ; cf. Corss. Ausspr. 1, 109; Mai.; 3, 2; Rom.; Marin. Fratr. Arv. p. 363; Bramb. p. 291 sq.), āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. and n.
for in-coco; from in and Sanscr. root kuk-, to take, grasp
.
Act., to lay the foundation of a thing, to begin, commence (syn. incipere; opp. absolvere, perficere; class.).
In gen.
With acc.: ut Phidias potest a primo instituere signum idque perficere, potest ab alio incohatum accipere et absolvere,; cf.: ut nemo pictor esset inventus, qui Coae Veneris eam partem, quam Apelles incohatam reliquisset, absolveret,; : statuam,: res in animis nostris,: quas res nos in consulatu nostro gessimus, attigit hic versibus atque incohavit,: philosophiam multis locis incohasti,: quod mihi nuper in Tusculano incohasti de oratoribus,: quod hic liber incohat,: hanc materiam,: abrupto, quem incohaverat, sermone,: esse videatur octonarium incohat,: referamus nos igitur ad eum, quem volumus incohandum et eloquentia informandum,: Favonius ver incohans,: incohandae vindemiae dies,: pulcherrimum facinus,: tum Stygio regi nocturnas incohat aras,i. e. begins to sacrifice,: reges plures incohantur, ne desint,are chosen,.—
With inf.: quam si mens fieri proponit et incohat ipsa,; ; .—
In partic., pregn. in the part. perf.: incŏhātus, a, um, only begun (opp. to finished, completed), unfinished, incomplete, imperfect (mostly Ciceron.): ne hanc incohatam transigam comoediam,: qui exaedificaret suam incohatam ignaviam,: quae adulescentulis nobis ex commentariolis nostris incohata ac rudia exciderunt,: cognitio manca atque incohata,: incohatum quiddam et confusum,: rem tam praeclaram incohatam relinquere,; cf. : perfecta anteponuntur incohatis,; cf.: hoc incohati cujusdam officii est, non perfecti,.—
Neutr., to begin, commence, take a beginning.
In gen. (post-class.): moris est, ut munus hujusmodi a proficiscentibus incohat,: incohante mense, and 33.— *
In partic., like infit, to begin to speak: post longa silentia rursus Incohat Ismene,. — Hence, incōhātē, adv., incipiently, incompletely, .

la:verb:incendo.gloss: to set on fire, burn, kindle
senses: to set on fire, burn, kindle
to light up with fire, make a fire upon
to make bright or shining, light up, brighten; adorn
to set on fire, inflame, excite, rouse, incite; incense, irritate
la:verb:incendo.html:
incendo, di, sum, 3 (archaic form of the
perf. subj. incensit = incenderit, sicut incepsit = inceperit, Paul. ex Müll.), v. a.
in-candeo; cf.: accendo and succendo
, to set fire to, to kindle, burn (freq. and class.; syn. inflammare).
Lit.: cupas taedā ac pice refertas incendunt,: tus et odores,; cf. odores,: lychnos,: oppida sua omnia, vicos, reliqua privata aedificia incendunt,: aedificia vicosque,: tabularium,: Capitolium,: naves omnes,: tamquam ipse suas incenderit aedes,: classem inflammari incendique jussit,: urbem,; cf. : quod primo incendendum Avaricum censuerat,: agros,: vepres,: cum ipse circumsessus paene incenderere,wast consumed,.—Absol.: nec incendit nisi ignis,.—
Transf.
To light up with fire, to make a fire upon: aras votis,i. e. in pursuance of vows,: altaria,.—
To heat, make hot: diem,: igne et tenuibus lignis fornacem incendemus,will heat, warm,.—
To make bright or shining, to brighten, illumine: ejusdem (solis) incensa radiis luna,; : maculosus et auro Squamam incendebat fulgor,: vivis digitos incendere gemmis, to make brilliant, i. e. to adorn, .—
Trop.
To kindle, inflame, set on fire; to fire, rouse, incite, excite; to irritate, incense (esp. freq. in pass.): ut mihi non solum tu incendere judicem, sed ipse ardere videaris,: iidem hominem perustum etiamnum gloria volunt incendere,: me ita vel cepit vel incendit, ut cuperem, etc.,: aliquem morando,: (aliquem) querelis,: in minime gratum spectaculum animo incenduntur,: Tyndariden incendit amor,: plebem largiundo atque pollicitando,: juventutem ad facinora,: bonorum animos,: animum cupidum inopiā,: cupiditatem alicujus,: odia improborum in nos,: tum pudor incendit vires et conscia virtus,inflames,: illam incendentem luctus,: clamore incendunt caelum, set on fire with, i. e. fill with, : regiam repentino luctu,: rabie jecur incendente feruntur Praecipites,: quibus incendi jam frigidus, aevo Laomedontiades possit,.—In pass.: nimis sermone hujus irā incendor,; ; cf.: incendor irā, esse ausam facere haec te injussu meo,: hisce ego illam dictis ita tibi incensam dabo, ut, etc.,: amore sum incensus,: (mulier) incensa odio pristino,: incendor quotidie magis non desiderio solum sed etiam incredibili fama virtutum admirabilium,: incensus studio,: iratus iste vehementer Sthenio et incensus hospitium renuntiat,: omnes incenduntur ad studia gloriā,; cf. : imperator incensus ad rem publicam bene gerendam,: Caesar ab eo (Crasso) in me esset incensus,: nulla mens est tam ad comprehendendam vim oratoris parata, quae possit incendi, nisi inflammatus ipse ad eam et ardens accesseris,: inimicitiis incensa contentio,: incensus calcaribus equus,.—Absol.: loquarne? incendam; taceam? instigem,: dumque petit petitur pariterque incendit et ardet,.—*
To enhance, raise: annonam (the price of corn), to produce a dearness or scarcity (shortly before: excandefaciebant), (cf. incendium, II. A.).—
To destroy, ruin, lay waste: si istuc conare ... tuum incendes genus,: campos,. — Hence, incensus, a, um, P. a., inflamed, burning, hot: profuit incensos aestus avertere ( = vehementissimos ardores febris), Forbig. ad loc.— In comp.: aether,.

incensus, a, um, adj.

la:verb:incedo.html:
in-cēdo, cessi, cessum (
sync. perf. incesti, ), 3, v. n. and a., to go, step, or march along at a measured pace (class.).
Lit.
In gen.
Neutr.: tenero et molli ingressu suspendimus gradum: non ambulamus, sed incedimus,: per vias,; cf.: socios per ipsos,: viā,: tota in urbe,: quacumque incederet,: quam taeter incedebat, quam truculentus,: incessit deinde, qua duxit praedae spes, victor exercitus,: etiam si pedes incedat, memorabilem fore,: servi pedibus, liberi non nisi equis incedunt. i. e. walk ... ride, ; cf.: incedunt pueri, pariterque ante ora parentum Frenatis lucent in equis,: a foro domum,: sessum impransum,: qui huc incedit,: ad me,: huc ad nos,; cf.: undique nuntii incedunt, qui afferrent, etc.,: ut ovans praeda onustus incederem,: vix incedo inanis, ne ire posse cum onere existumes,: quem modo decoratum ovantemque victoria incedentem vidistis,; : claro honore,: omnibus laetitiis,: incedunt per ora vestra magnifici,: ego quae divum incedo regina,who walk majestic as, who am,; cf. : matrona incedit census induta nepotum, (4, 12): ut mea Luxuria Nemesis fluat ut que per urbem Incedat donis conspicienda meis,.—

In partic., in milit. lang., to move forwards, advance, march: barbari in perculsos Romanos acrius incedere,: in erumpentes,: cohortes paulatim incedere jubet,: munito agmine,: agmen reliquum incedere coepit,: segnius Hispanorum signa incedebant,: Sabini usque ad portas urbis populantes incessere,: propius incedentes,: quod gnarum duci incessitque itineri et proelio paratus, (Ritter, but Halm omits paratus).—
Trop.
In gen. (rare): malitiae lenonis contra incedam,will encounter,: facilius ad inventionem animus incedet si, etc.,will proceed to, Orell. N. cr. —
In partic.
To triumph over, exult over; with dat.: meo nunc superbus incedis malo,: ille superbus incedet victis rivalibus,.—
Of inanim. and abstr. subjects, to come to, happen to, befall, attack, seize one; to approach, arrive, appear, occur (perh. not in Cic.); constr. with dat., acc., in and acc., or absol.
With dat. (so most freq.): exercitui omni tantus incessit ex incommodo dolor, ut, etc.,: magnus omnium incessit timor animis,: mulieres, quibus belli timor insolitus incesserat, etc., Kritz N. cr.; : gravior cura patribus incessit,: incedebat enim deterrimo cuique licentia,: cupido incessit animo,; : si sterilitas annorum incessit hominibus,; .—
With acc.: ipsum ingens cupido incesserat Tarenti potiundi,: timor patres incessit, ne, etc.,; ; ; 7, 39, 4 et saep.: indignatio hostes incessit,: adversa valetudo aliquem,: ingens animos desperatio incessit,; : stupor omnes et admiratio incessit,: cupido incessit aliquem (with acc. and inf.), ; .—
With in and acc.: vis morbi, pestilentia incedit in castra, in Poenos Romanosque,: pestilentia incesserat pari clade in Romanos

Poenosque, .—

Absol.: nova nunc religio unde istaec incessit?: tantus eo facto timor incessit,; Auct. B. Alex. 7: postquam tenebrae incedebant,; cf.: ubi crepusculum incesserit,: ubi tempestas incessit,: frigora,: siccitates,: lascivia atque superbia incessere,: ubi Romam legati venere, tanta commutatio incessit, uti, etc.,: religio deinde incessit, vitio eos creatos,: ubi pro modestia ac pudore ambitio et vis incedebat,: haud invito imperatore ea fieri occultus rumor incedebat,went abroad, spread about,fin.

incesso, cessīvi (less freq. cessi. Tac H. 2, 23; 3, 77; ), 3, v. a.
incedo
,

Lit.: quae (pars corporis) cum jaculis saxisque incesseretur,: vagos suos pro hostibus lapidibus incessebant,; cf.: infestis digitis ora et oculos,; : feras argenteis vasis incessivere tum primum noxii,: telorum lapidumque jactu,: a pueris ii more quodam gentis saxis globosis, funda mare apertum incessentes exercebantur, Weissenb. ad loc.: jaculis et voce superba Tecta incessentem,; .—Absol.: saevis telis,: stercore et caeno,. —
Trop., to attack, assault, esp. with words, to reprove, reproach, accuse: reges dictis protervis,: aliquem verbis amaris,; cf. : aliquem conviciis,; : adversarios maledictis,: senatum diris exsecrationibus,: Sallustium noto epigrammate,: juvenes objurgatione justa,: nomen hominis acerba cavillatione,: aliquem bello,: aliquem poenis,: aliquem criminibus,to accuse him,: aliquem occultis suspicionibus,: aliquem ut tumidiorem,: aliquem ut impium erga parentes,: nomen ut argumentum morum incessit,; cf.: aliquem tamquam superbe saeveque egisset,: sermonem cum risu aliquos incessentem,: si aut nationes totae aut ordines incessantur,: paucitatem, conspirationem, vilitatem, gratiam,: ne incesse moras,.—Of a disease: pestilentia incesserat pari clade in Romanos Poenosque,: tanta incesserit in ea castra vis morbi,.—Of fear, etc.: timor deinde patres incessit, ne, etc.,: super haec timor incessit Sabini belli,: tantus terror Tarquinium incessit,.—Of other feelings: cupido incessit animos juvenum, sciscitandi, etc.,: tanta admiratio miseratioque viri incessit homines, ut, etc.,: cura incesserat patres,: incessit omnes stupor et admiratio,.

la:noun:incendium.html:
incendĭum, ĭi, n.
incendo
,
a burning, fire, conflagration.
Lit. (freq. and class.; equally common in sing. and plur.): incendium facere,to set fire to,; : excitare, restinguere, (v. under II.): in ipso urbis incendio,: frumentum flumine atque incendio corruperunt,: omnia incendiis vastare,; cf.: nihil cogitant nisi caedes, nisi incendia, nisi rapinas,: si incendium in arce fuerit,: si janua tenebitur incendio,: cunctos qui proelio superfuerant, incendium hausit,: neglecta solent incendia sumere vires,; cf. : Aetna nocturnis mirus incendiis,: vivendum est illic, ubi nulla incendia,: incendia praedandi causa facere,: fortuita incendia,.—
Transf.
In gen., fire, burning, heat (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): siderum,: Auster Africae incendia cum serenitate affert,: stomachi,.—
Concr., a firebrand, torch (poet.), ; .—
Trop., fire, flame, heat, glow, vehemence (class.; a favorite trope of Cic.).
In gen.: si quod esset in suas fortunas incendium excitatum, id se non aquā sed ruinā restincturum,; cf. : miseriarum,: invidiae incendio conflagrare,: incendio alieni judicii conflagrare,: res cogit, huic tanto incendio succurrere omnes, qui, etc., Asin. Poll. ap. : populare,: annonae,a raising of the price of corn,; Ps.-.—
Esp., the fire of passion: ita mihi in pectore atque in corde facit amor incendium, 3, 4, 3: cupiditatum incendiis inflammatus,: restinctis jam animorum incendiis,: oratione concitare,: abstruso pectus ejus flagravit incendio (i. e. dolore),: militaris tumultus,: aliae Satyris incendia mitia praebent,enkindle, inflame,: movere,.

la:verb:incito.gloss: to set in rapid motion, hasten, urge forwards, speed up, accelerate, quicken
senses: to set in rapid motion, hasten, urge forwards, speed up, accelerate, quicken
to cause to grow larger; augment, increase; enhance; intensify
to incite, encourage, stimulate, rouse, evoke, excite, spur on; inspire
la:verb:incito.html:
in-cĭto, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to set in rapid motion, to hasten, urge forwards; and with se, to put one's self in rapid motion, to hasten, rush (freq. and class.).
Lit.
In gen.: vehementius equos incitare,: saxa per pronum, Dietsch: hastas,: stellarum motus tum incitantur, tum retardantur,: naves longas remis,; cf.: lintres magno sonitu remorum incitatae,: navigio remis incitato,: alii ex castris sese incitant,sally out,; cf.: cum ex alto se aestus incitavisset,had rushed in,; and: quo major vis aquae se incitavisset,: duabus ex partibus sese (naves) in eam (navem) incitaverant, ; cf. .—Prov.: incitare currentem, to spur a willing horse, i. e. to urge a person who does not need urging, ; cf. ; v. curro.—
In partic., to cause to grow larger, i. e. to augment, increase, to promote the growth of (not ante-Aug.; cf. excito, I. B.): hibernis (Enipeus amnis) incitatus pluviis,swollen,: frequentibus fossuris terra permiscetur, ut incitari vitis possit,; . fin.; 3, 21, 7.—
Trop., to incite, encourage, stimulate, rouse, excite, spur on.
In gen.: aliquem imitandi cupiditate,: quibus (causis) mentes aut incitantur aut reflectuntur,: animos, opp. sedare,: ipsum ingenium diligentia etiam ex tarditate incitat,: quorum studio legendi meum scribendi studium in dies incitatur,: quamquam ea incitatur in civitate ratio vivendi,: stultas cogitationes,: quoniam ad hanc voluntatem ipsius naturae stimulis incitamur,; cf.: juvenes ad studium et ad laborem,: aliquem ad servandum genus hominum,: multa Caesarem ad id bellum incitabant,: aliquem ad bellum atque arma,: aliquem ad amplissimam spem,: cujus voluptatis avidae libidines temere et effrenate ad potiundum incitarentur,: incitabant (animum ferocem) praeterea conrupti civitatis mores,: cum tibia lumbos incitat,. —
In partic.
To inspire. nam terrae vis Pythiam Delphis incitabat, naturae Sibyllam, : mente incitati,; .—
In a bad sense, to excite, arouse, stir up: neque enim desunt, qui istos in me atque in optimum quemque incitent,; cf. : et consules senatum in tribunum et tribunus populum in consules incitabat,: his vocibus cum in se magis incitarent dictatorem,: opifices facile contra vos incitabuntur, (shortly before, concitentur); : milites nostri pristini diei perfidiā incitati,: civitas ob eam rem incitata,: judices,.—
(Acc. to I. B.) To augment, increase, enhance: consuetudo exercitatioque et intellegendi prudentiam acuit et eloquendi celeritatem incitat,; so, caelibum poenas,.—Hence, incĭtātus, a, um, P. a. (set in rapid motion; hence), swiftly running, flowing, sailing, flying, etc.; in gen., rapid, swift.
Lit.: imperator equo incitato se in hostes immittens,at full speed,: equo incitato, (for which: citato equo; v. cito): milites cursu incitato in summo colle ab hostibus conspiciebantur,advancing rapidly,; cf. in the foll. B.: mundi incitatissima conversio, (shortly before: conversio concitatior).—
Trop.: cursus in oratione incitatior,; cf. so of speech: Herodotus sine ullis salebris quasi sedatus amnis fluit: Thucydides incitatior fertur,.—Adv.: incĭtātē (acc. to B.), of speech, quickly, rapidly, violently: fluit incitatius,: quod incitatius feratur (locutio),.

in-cŭbo, ŭi, ĭtum, āre (rarely āvi, ātum, in the sense of to brood), 1, v. n. and a.
, to lie in a place or upon a thing (class.).
